lawfulRepositoryConvention.convention: The sole lawful home of direct SQL against an aggregate's tables is that aggregate's EK-3 sole-writer repository file: src/workflow-kernel/persistence/<kebab(AggregateName)>-repository.ts (FactoryRun -> src/workflow-kernel/persistence/factory-run-repository.ts). Every direct-SQL statement against those tables in any other file is FORBIDDEN bypass SQL.
lawfulRepositoryConvention.tableBelongsRule: table t belongs to aggregate A (prefix p) iff t === p || t === p + 's' || t.startsWith(p + '_'); anchored at the table-name start, so predecessor composites (factory_lifecycle_runs, factory_workplaces, factory_runtime_mode) belong to no successor aggregate
lawfulRepositoryConvention.derivation: The aggregate set is exactly the frozen universe's aggregates (frozen-inputs/transition-universe.json aggregates[].name) and the projection-table set is exactly the census PROJECTION class (frozen-inputs/authority-census.json tables[t].tableClass === 'PROJECTION'); measure-complexity.mjs re-proves both equalities on every run, so this declared map cannot drift from the frozen inputs. The table prefixes themselves are frozen HERE (this budget is the spec-frozen authority for successor physical table naming per aggregate).
lawfulRepositoryConvention.splitContract: For every dimension that counts SQL statements against new-kernel aggregates (authority.decisionReaderStatements, authority.decisionWriterStatements, authority.projectionAuthorityReads): lawful = statements inside the owning repository file of an aggregate whose tables they touch; bypass = the same statements anywhere else. The target binds on bypass == 0; the lawful column is unconstrained by these dimensions (bounded instead by authority.mutableOwnerFanInFiles max 1 writer file per table and authority.mutableOwnerAggregates exact 13 authority kinds). Before src/workflow-kernel exists the vector emits bypass = frozen-census total, lawful = 0 (no lawful owner exists on the predecessor tree), so --check binds on the bypass column the moment the kernel lands. Adding a projection table name is a recorded tightening; removing one reopens EK-1.
lawfulRepositoryConvention.revisionPolicy: Adding an aggregate or an aggregate table prefix reopens EK-1 (authority-topology delta); renaming a prefix is a budget revision requiring an independent-verifier-approved measured complexity delta before code is written.

kernelCompositionConvention.convention: The successor-tree binding conventions for the eight census-frozen dimensions (budget rev3). (1) Sole implementation surfaces are identified by frozen basename stems inside src/workflow-kernel/**: the obligation consumer, the role-binding compiler and the prompt/context assembler each live in exactly ONE production file whose basename contains the frozen stem. (2) Workshop-owned scheduler implementations are production files ANYWHERE in the scanned scopes (src/**, scripts/**, tracker-view/**) whose basename matches the frozen schedulerFilePattern. (3) Relation kinds and non-aggregate authority kinds are declared as namespaced kind literals in src/workflow-kernel/domain/** ('relation:<PascalName>' resp. 'authority:<PascalName>'), the same declaration style the protocol vocabularies use. (4) Aggregate owner repositories are the lawfulRepositoryConvention repository files under src/workflow-kernel/persistence/.
kernelCompositionConvention.derivation: relationNames is re-proved on every driver run against the plan's '## Target logical model' table (docs/plans/EVENT-PROJECTED-KERNEL-GREENFIELD-REFACTORING-PLAN.md; the plan's law: 'The new schema must contain exactly the logical relations below') and cross-checked against the frozen universe: every frozen-universe aggregate except CognitionTransport must be one of the 22 (CognitionTransport is the universe's own sanctioned exception — 'replaceable transport behind the provider-send obligation (not an aggregate owner)', transition-universe.json aggregates[CognitionTransport]) and must NOT appear in relationNames. nonAggregateAuthorityNames is re-proved to exactly equal the frozen universe's nonAggregateAuthorities names. The stems and the scheduler pattern are frozen HERE (this budget is the spec-frozen authority for the counted surface names, mirroring lawfulRepositoryConvention).
kernelCompositionConvention.bindingContract: Before src/workflow-kernel exists the eight re-bound dimensions emit the frozen-census/universe value as the non-binding predecessor baseline column with the kernel-scope column 0/target-only (the established fail-loudly discipline: a dimension whose measured artifact does not exist never silently passes). Once src/workflow-kernel exists the same commands measure the live tree and the targets bind: authority.mutableOwnerFanInFiles = maximum per-aggregate distinct direct-SQL writer files (max 1, the owning repository); authority.mutableOwnerAggregates = repository files under src/workflow-kernel/persistence/ matching *-repository.ts plus distinct authority:<Name> literals in the declaration scope (exact 13 = 9 + 4); authority.authoritativeRelationKinds = distinct relation:<Name> literals in the declaration scope (exact 22); the three sole-implementation stems count files (exact 1 each); workshops.ownedSchedulerImplementations = schedulerFilePattern files anywhere (max 0); debt.temporaryLegacySurfaces = frozen-census delete-disposition writer statements whose file still exists under production paths (ratchets to 0 exactly when the EK-8 legacy-zero deletion completes).
kernelCompositionConvention.revisionPolicy: Renaming a stem, the scheduler pattern or a literal prefix is a budget revision requiring an independent-verifier-approved measured complexity delta before code is written; adding a relation or a non-aggregate authority reopens EK-1 (authority-topology delta); removing one is a recorded tightening.
